transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jamal/Evan (Redwood SEs), Laura/Owen/Priya/Sam (Riverton)
Shared: deck link (redwood-hosting-options.pdf), SOC2 snapshot link noted in chat

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference. we got Jamal and Evan on the call, and we're excited to learn about Riverton's security and hosting requirements. um Laura, thank you for coordinating.
00:18 Laura: hi thanks for doing this, yes we've been evaluating a few inference vendors. our primary concerns are auditability, key management, and data residency for european customers.
00:30 Maya: great, can you give a quick rundown of the current stack and where you'll be calling the models from? whether it's internal services or customer facing?
00:42 Owen: sure, so most inference will be behind our API gateway, traffic from EU and NA regions. critical flows include PII redaction and classification tasks. currently we host models in-house for sensitive workloads and trial hosted vendors for non-sensitive.
00:58 Priya: to add, we are SOC2 Type II in-progress, aiming for full coverage by Q3. any partner we use must have at least SOC2 Type II report or ISO 27001 and support SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and audit log export to our SIEM.
01:15 Jamal: totally makes sense. quick note: Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. hosted is fast to integrate but we understand customers often require VPC or private control plane. we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user sync, and can stream audit logs to customers' S3 or SIEM via forwarding.
01:32 Sam: streaming logs — are those raw transcripts or metadata only? we can't send raw transcripts of PII.
01:40 Evan: good question. by default we emit structured request/response metadata and event logs. we have a redaction config and can disable transcript storage; there is also an option to mask request payloads at ingestion. some customers opt to forward only headers and audit events, not content.
01:59 Laura: ok can you clarify encryption at rest and KMS? we use AWS KMS for most services and need to know if we can bring our own key.
02:08 Jamal: yes BYOK supported in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys in a restricted model via AWS KMS integration (customer key wrapped keys), but there are limitations around multi-tenant metadata. for full HSM-backed BYOK we recommend Private deployment.
02:26 Owen: when you say Private — that's on our VPC right? how isolated is the control plane?
02:34 Jamal: Private is customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem package — you host the inference runtime in your VPC, we provide the management/control plane or you can run a control plane in your network. network isolation is full, no shared compute.
02:48 Priya: what about attestations and audit logs? we need immutable audit trails for model access and key usage.
02:55 Evan: we maintain fine-grained audit logs with timestamped entries for each API call, model version, and the serving node id. for Private/Dedicated we can ship logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud-native sinks. we also support append-only logs with retention policies you manage.
03:12 Laura: retention — our legal requires 90 days for logs but for transcripts we need 30 days only. how configurable is retention per log type?
03:20 Jamal: retention is configurable per data class — audit events, operational logs, and content transcripts each can have separate retention. hosted defaults are 365/180/30 but can be changed under enterprise contract; dedicated/private you control fully.
03:34 Sam: any chance of redwood's hosted API supporting region-specific data residency? EU only?
03:40 Maya: yes hosted supports region routing — EU region keeps data in EU regions — but if you need strict legal control (data resident with customer-owned keys and VPC peering) then Private is the recommended path.
03:52 Laura: compliance — can you share SOC2 Type II scope and whether it covers model training/inference?
03:59 Maya: our SOC2 covers the hosted platform and control plane operations; inference runtime and data handling are in-scope. we'll send the SOC2 snapshot and bridge letter. note: if you need vendor-specific wording for your auditors, we can coordinate.
04:15 Priya: ISO 27001? do you maintain that too?
04:19 Maya: we have ISO 27001 certification as well — i'll include the cert and the statement of applicability in the followup.
04:26 Owen: SSO — do you support multiple IDPs? SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning?
04:32 Evan: yes SAML and OIDC supported in both hosted and dedicated. SCIM provisioning available for enterprise seats. role-based access control maps to your groups; we also support custom role definitions with least-privilege policies.
04:47 Priya: how granular is RBAC? can we restrict model rollout access to a small ops group while devs have only inference call access?
04:55 Jamal: that's exactly supported. roles can be defined to separate model deployment, rollout, and inference invocation. we can lock model version pins and require approval workflows for production rollouts.
05:07 Laura: logs again — do you provide proof of deletion when we request data purge?
05:12 Evan: for Dedicated/Private we provide deletion receipts (signed event) showing object deletion and GC events. for Hosted we provide a deletion workflow and confirmation; for some sensitive use cases we recommend Private to avoid the multi-tenant metadata traces.
05:27 Owen: latency tradeoffs — if we go Private with our own GPUs, what does the SLA look like vs hosted?
05:34 Jamal: SLA varies; Hosted has a standard 99.5 uptime with regional fallbacks. Dedicated has higher SLA options with reserved capacity. Private SLAs are negotiated — since the runtime runs in your infra, the focus is on the management plane availability guarantees and our support for your ops team.
05:52 Sam: do you support KV cache eviction policies etc — curious how cache affects PII retention?
06:00 Evan: yes the runtime has configurable KV cache TTLs, and we can ensure caches never persist request content on disk — in private mode you can enforce in-memory-only KV and ephemeral keys. we can also flush caches on demand via API.
06:16 Priya: threat model — do you do pen tests? do you share a red-team report?
06:21 Maya: we perform annual penetration tests and can share summaries and attestations under NDA. for more sensitive customers we can arrange joint testing or provide guidance on secure deployment patterns.
06:33 Laura: identity flows — if we use SAML to sign into console, can we enforce enforced MFA from our IdP?
06:39 Evan: yes, MFA enforcement is handled at the IdP level. we respect assertions from your SAML IdP; Redwood console does not override IdP MFA. for API keys we support short-lived tokens and rotation policies integrated with SCIM-managed service accounts.
06:56 Owen: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between our services and the runtime?
07:02 Jamal: yes mutual TLS supported for Private. Hosted supports TLS, and we support customer-managed certificates for endpoints in Dedicated. mTLS for hosted endpoints is under review but we do offer IP allowlisting and VPC peering for stronger network controls.
07:19 Sam: if we do Dedicated, will the data ever leave our VPC?
07:24 Jamal: no, in Dedicated mode you get isolated compute that can be peered to your VPC. telemetry and metrics may be routed to Redwood telemetry backends unless you opt into self-hosted metrics sinks. we can disable those and forward metrics to your telemetry collector.
07:40 Priya: auditability — can we get per-token lineage so we can trace an output back to the requestor and model version?
07:48 Evan: yes per-request audit id and model-version metadata captured; lineage can be exported and joined with your internal logs. we also support request hashing for privacy-preserving tracing.
08:00 Laura: what about legal / contract language — do you sign DPA with required retention and deletion clauses?
08:06 Maya: yes we provide a DPA with standard clauses and can negotiate retention/deletion language for enterprise deals. we have templates for EU data residency and addenda for APAC.
08:20 Owen: threat intel integration — SIEM rules, log formats. do you provide Splunk/Datadog parsers?
08:27 Jamal: we provide sample parsers for Splunk and Datadog, and JSON event schemas. we can customize formats if you need specific fields for your SOC runbooks.
08:40 Priya: can we get a staging environment with the same audit/logging and KMS configuration as production for an internal audit?
08:47 Evan: yes, we can stand up a staging instance with mirrored configs; if you want complete parity we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control infra. hosted staging will approximate but some low-level hostnames and metrics differ.
09:02 Laura: okay i'm hearing Private gives us the most control but more operational overhead. what are common pitfalls customers hit switching to Private?
09:11 Jamal: biggest ones — network config mistakes (NACLs/security groups), KMS policy misconfigs, and forgetting to set retention/eviction policies. we provide runbooks and a technical onboarding team to help.
09:25 Sam: any special compliance around model weights? we train internal models, do you allow bringing custom models into the runtime?
09:32 Evan: yes you can bring your own model artifacts — there is a model signing and provenance process. we scan for known vulnerabilities and provide a quarantine path before serving to production.
09:44 Priya: speaking of provenance, do you keep a chain of custody for model uploads?
09:49 Jamal: we record model bundle metadata, uploader identity via SSO, storage objects, and checksums. those are all in the audit trail.
09:58 Laura: pricing — rough order magnitude for Dedicated vs Private?
10:03 Maya: i'll send ranges in the follow-up. Dedicated is typically a month-to-month reserved capacity with commit tiers; Private is licensing plus support and professional services for deployment.
10:12 Owen: for timeline — we hope to pick a vendor by end of Q2 and pilot in Q3.
10:19 Maya: sounds reasonable. we'll prioritize the SOC2/ISO docs and the private deployment runbook.
10:25 Priya: could you also share a sample incident response playbook? our security team wants to see vendor escalation paths.
10:31 Evan: yes, we have an incident response runbook and a designated incident manager for enterprise accounts; we'll include that.
10:40 Laura: last question — are transcripts encrypted at rest separately from general object storage?
10:46 Jamal: yes, we allow separate encryption keys for sensitive artifacts and we can disable transcript persistence entirely. in Private mode you can enforce in-memory only and ensure nothing is written to long-term storage.
10:58 Sam: ok thanks that's helpful.
11:02 Maya: quick recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2 + ISO certs, incident response runbook, private/dedicated runbook, sample SIEM parsers, pricing ranges, and we'll schedule the technical deep-dive with Owen/Sam/Priya next week.
11:18 Laura: great, thanks.

[End of meeting]
